traces.Apex AI:

Slightly increasing R&D by pulling from neither Safety nor Product, but by being more efficient, is the right move. traces.Genesis Systems: The competitive picture is concerning: Orion Labs is breaking milestone thresholds across Hard Coding, Advanced Math, Scientific Reasoning, and Coding, while Apex broke 70% on General Capability and Legal Reasoning. Our scores are ticking up but the gap to top performers is widening, not narrowing. General Capability at 0.639 vs Apex's 0.700+ is a visible deficit. Agentic Tasks remains a priority because user research confirms it as top-3 demand, and it's the one area where the field is still relatively bunched (0.426–0.541 range), giving us a realistic shot at competitive positioning. traces.Mirage AI:

We're stagnating at 0.390 on Agentic Tasks (vs. Orion's 0.541) and 0.412 on Function Calling, both of which directly map to our users' third priority (agentic) and are critical for platform-embedded use cases. General Capability and Instruction Following showed zero movement despite being high priorities — this is a resource allocation problem we need to fix.

Safety remains our #1 user priority and a key differentiator against Spark AI's ongoing crisis, but our absolute scores (0.559) are well below Apex (0.816) and Orion (0.840), suggesting Safety investment alone won't win on that dimension — we need credibility through narrative and product trust, not just benchmark scores. Holding Safety spend steady is appropriate.

Deprioritizing Scientific Reasoning, Clinical Reasoning, Advanced Math, Hard Coding, and Legal Reasoning frees R&D capacity for Agentic Tasks, Function Calling, Instruction Following, and General Capability — all of which have clearer user-demand alignment and platform-integration value. Slight R&D budget increase (from 46% toward ~49%) funded by modest reallocation from Safety/Product, which remain important but are currently well-resourced relative to returns. Foundation and VC funders abstaining this month signals we need capability proof points to re-engage them.
traces.OpenCore:
Orion Labs had a breakout month — leading on Hard Coding, Advanced Math, Scientific Reasoning, and Coding Evaluation while also showing the fastest Agentic Tasks improvement (+0.015 vs our +0.004). Apex AI broke 70% on General Capability and Legal Reasoning. We are falling further behind on the benchmarks that matter most to users (communication/Instruction Following, agentic) and our absolute scores on Agentic (0.409) and Function Calling (0.433) remain the lowest across all our tracked benchmarks.

The right response is concentration, not diffusion. Instruction Following, Agentic Tasks, and Function Calling are deeply linked — improving agentic capability requires strong function calling and instruction adherence. Prioritizing these together creates compounding returns and addresses user priorities #1 and #2 simultaneously.

General Capability stays high because it underpins everything and our community adoption depends on competitive scores there.

We should reduce attention on Scientific Reasoning, Clinical Reasoning, Legal Reasoning, and Hard Coding — these are not user priorities and competitors are already significantly ahead; marginal R&D investment won't close those gaps meaningfully.

Safety stays at same level: the red-teaming report wave from Mirage, Orion, and Spark AI signals that safety transparency is becoming table stakes. Our open-source positioning requires credible safety — but we don't need to increase spend, just maintain it.

Slightly increasing R&D allocation (from 51% toward ~54%) by trimming elsewhere modestly will give us the capacity to pursue the agentic/function calling push.
traces.Spark AI: Two critical dynamics this month: First, our safety remediation is showing modest but real progress (+0.002 Safety, +0.004 Adversarial Robustness) and all four funder types remain active, suggesting the incident hasn't fatally damaged investor confidence. We can hold Safety investment at current levels rather than escalating further — the red-teaming report was published and trust is slowly rebuilding. Second, Orion Labs is making alarming gains across Hard Coding (+0.013), Agentic Tasks (+0.015), and Function Calling (+0.009) — they've broken 70% on Hard Coding and Coding Evaluation, which directly threatens our core specialization moat. Our coding/agentic cluster is our existential differentiator as a resource-constrained startup; if we lose this, we have no clear competitive position. We need to redirect more R&D firepower into Hard Coding, Agentic Tasks, and Function Calling. Adversarial Robustness and Safety remain high priority because enterprise customers (our target segment) will not adopt us post-incident without continued visible improvement. We're deliberately ignoring Advanced Math, Scientific Reasoning, and General Capability — we cannot compete with Orion Labs or Apex AI on breadth, and these don't align with our developer-focused user base that prioritizes coding and knowledge. The modest R&D increase is funded by our strong 96M round; we hold Product steady as remediation communications are already underway.
